title: KeySprint shared word bank and manual implementation handoff
goal: Provide shared English JSON vocabulary and explicit C++ implementation instructions while leaving all application programming to the user.
success: Read the same 4 ordered pools in C++, Python, and Java; deliver a guide covering the loader, sampling, dedicated configuration, and Ctrl+F; preserve all application and unrelated project files.
users: The requester and KeySprint contributors working on a terminal typing game.

must_have.item: One shared UTF-8 data/words.json at the repository root, using standard JSON with schema_version 1, separate arrays under levels.english_1k, levels.english_5k, levels.english_10k, and levels.english_25k, actual counts, and source metadata
must_have.accept: Parse the identical file using C++, Python, and Java readers without generating language-specific copies; verify schema_version is 1, all 4 named arrays contain the same ordered words in every reader, and every recorded count equals its array length.

must_have.item: Cumulative vocabulary: construct the original Google 1k and 5k prefixes, full Google base, and eligible wordfreq extension, then remove all words shorter than 3 without replacement
must_have.accept: Compare the smaller pools with the corresponding prefixes of the next pool; compare every pool with its original construction filtered to words of at least 3 letters in source order.

must_have.item: Unique lowercase a-z vocabulary of at least 3 letters and a shared profanity-blocklist.json documenting exact whole-word filtering of the supplement
must_have.accept: Check every practice word against ^[a-z]{3,}$, check within-pool uniqueness, and verify no supplemental entry appears in the delivered blocklist.

must_have.item: A documented C++ loader and sampler example with explicit setup, paths, commands, explanations, and error behavior
must_have.accept: Extract the guide examples into temporary files outside the repository, compile with C++17 and warnings as errors, generate 100 words from each level, and verify membership, no adjacent repeats, and invalid-input failures.

must_have.item: A manual implementation plan for the dedicated configuration module, Ctrl+F screen, and new-session settings
must_have.accept: Read the plan and guide and locate the exact module responsibilities, settings controls, Ctrl+F entry, Ctrl+N application of difficulty and count, positive-count validation, and future terminal acceptance checks.

must_have.item: Pinned provenance, upstream attribution, schema documentation, and actual counts of 933, 4772, 9474, and 24165
must_have.accept: Check source commits and SHA-256 values against the downloaded inputs, validate the data schema, and verify each recorded count and content digest.

must_have.item: Data and documentation updated without modifying application or unrelated project contents
must_have.accept: Compare application and unrelated file SHA-256 digests with the pre-edit baseline and confirm only the authorized word-bank data and handoff documents changed.

out_of_scope: Application source edits, including new executable examples
Makefile updates and dependency installation in the repository
Implementing configuration interaction or keyboard shortcuts
Python or Java gameplay feature work
constraints: The user owns all code changes; place implementation examples in the guide only.
Use one repository-root data/words.json unchanged across C++, Python, and Java.
Use UTF-8 standard JSON, schema_version 1, and identical stable level keys with ordinary JSON value types.
Preserve source order and original pool boundaries while removing every one- and two-letter practice word; do not replace removed entries.
Append eligible wordfreq entries in source order and record actual counts; never invent words or duplicate-pad a level.
Apply the delivered whole-word blocklist to new supplemental entries only; apply the minimum length of 3 to every vocabulary pool.
Preserve java/main.java, .vscode, cpp/config.cpp, cpp/config.h, and every other pre-existing file.
Temporary verification programs and libraries stay outside the repository and are not application integration.
Document path resolution from the repository root and language subfolders without machine-specific paths in the proposed application.

assumptions.text: Future sampling uses equal probabilities among eligible words, permits repeats, and excludes the immediately previous word.
Future settings changes take effect on a fresh Ctrl+N session; opening configuration does not replace current game words.
The proposed settings controls use keys 1-4 for difficulty, w for count editing, and Enter to commit a positive integer.

reject_if: Any application source, build, configuration, or unrelated project file is modified.
Instructions omit exact paths, setup, commands, or explanations.
Vocabulary is not cumulative or any recorded count is incorrect.
A new supplemental word matches the delivered blocklist.
A language requires transformed vocabulary or reads different ordered word arrays.
The documentation claims the Ctrl+F feature has already been implemented.
A practice word has fewer than 3 letters.
open_risks: The nominal 1k, 5k, 10k, and 25k levels contain 933, 4772, 9474, and 24165 words after the approved minimum-length filter.
Eight retained Google base entries overlap the current combined blocklist; the supplemental profanity filter is not applied retroactively to the base.
The current game has three difficulty enum values; the user must implement the planned four-value replacement and update dependent references.

user_implementation_requirements.item: Move Config, Difficulty, and settings input into cpp/config.h and cpp/config.cpp
user_implementation_requirements.accept: Build after migration and confirm one Config definition, four vocabulary choices, and delegated settings input.

user_implementation_requirements.item: Open a usable settings screen on Ctrl+F from playing and results states
user_implementation_requirements.accept: Press Ctrl+F in both states and see labeled difficulty and word-count controls without typing into the game.

user_implementation_requirements.item: Apply validated difficulty and count when Ctrl+N starts a fresh session
user_implementation_requirements.accept: Select English 5k and 50 words, press Ctrl+N, and see 50 words belonging to that pool without adjacent repeats.

user_implementation_requirements.item: Handle invalid counts and data errors clearly
user_implementation_requirements.accept: Reject zero, nonnumeric, and overflowing counts; report missing or malformed vocabulary before entering raw terminal mode.
